The Cook condition is
that $t\mapsto\Psi_t^\eta(f)$ is norm-$C^1$ on
$[1,\infty)$ and, for constants $C_{\eta,f}\ge0$ and
$\epsilon_{\eta,f}>0$,
$$\left\|\frac{d}{dt}\Psi_t^\eta(f)\right\|\le C_{\eta,f}(1+t)^{-1-\epsilon_{\eta,f}}\qquad(t\ge1).$$

\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$ and
$\mathcal F_a(H)=\{(\Psi_n)_{n\ge0}:\Psi_n\in H_a^{(n)},\
\sum_n\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, with the componentwise inner product.

The positive-power tail makes the curve Cauchy at infinity and gives the explicit norm-limit rate.
Pointwise norm limits of the supplied linear approximant maps are linear on the packet domain.
Convergence of pairwise inner products to the Fock pairing makes the limit map norm-preserving.
The isometry on the packet domain extends uniquely to its Hilbert-space closure by completeness.
